capabilities_done: slice 1: open (package -> folio snapshot), revision-checked submit through an instance-owned provider registry, atomic save with destination re-read, cancellation + budgets, one Observe frame per operation, session-consumer
slice 2: injected GrantPort/CommitPort/JobPort/Clock, idempotency keys + canonical receipts, outcome-unknown reconcile (exactly once), bounded admission, shutdown drain, export_checkpoint

slice 3 lazy source (src/source.rs): open keeps the package as a Read+Seek stream behind PackageReader (structure and every entry checksum verified in bounded 1 MiB chunks); the document and the entries that must be preserved verbatim (opaque, unlisted) are read through a second logical cursor over the same stream and verified against the manifest SHA-256; asset and preview bodies are NOT read at open (tile digests are checked against the manifest only). Resident at rest: document, preserved unknown entries, host-supplied previews

slice 3 on-demand reads: save/export pull each asset from the source one at a time (PackageReader::read_asset, SHA-256 verified, bounded by the writer's max and the manifest's declared size) and source previews lazily; the real cause of a failed read (hash_mismatch, io, canceled) is reported instead of asset_absent; the written file becomes the new source (old handle released) and in-memory sessions (open_bytes) release their copy on first save

slice 3 host previews: Session::set_previews(rendered_for_revision, Vec<PreviewImage>) validates (dimensions, byte length, colour tag, unique content, <= MAX_SUPPLIED_PREVIEWS, total bytes) and accepts only the current revision (stale_revision otherwise); supplied previews replace the source's at the next save/export at that revision; anything rendered for another revision is dropped and counted (SaveReceipt/Checkpoint.previews_dropped); supplied previews are released once written. PixelFormat/PreviewImage/PreviewInfo re-exported so hosts need no package dependency

R3 lineage (63c1f5d): propose_checked now requires the provider's successor to equal the live document plus new values at exactly the declared revision-update addresses (mask_property on both documents, compare, revision aligned); a provider that prepared from an edited copy is refused with SessionError::ProposalNotDerived (code proposal_not_derived, Observe Failure(Validation)) before publish or any commit-port call

streaming save (943a0d2): LazyAssets implements package AssetStream (raw entries stream from their byte range in the source through a forked Handle cursor, constant memory; zstd/shuffle_zstd entries decode via PackageReader::read_asset as one blob; open is repeatable, one reader at a time; the real cause is kept in take_failure); save_inner uses save_atomic_streaming (package re-verifies the temp from disk before the atomic replace), gather_previews/write_options/writer_cause shared with export; export_checkpoint stays on write_package_with (a Checkpoint is an in-memory verified package by contract); the destination is still reopened as the new source (Handle::pair, new raw cursor)

R5 receipt eviction (82a97b4): Budgets::receipt_policy ReceiptPolicy::{EvictAcknowledged (default), RefuseWhenFull}; the table never exceeds max_receipts; the oldest ACKNOWLEDGED committed receipt (handed to the caller by a submit result, a replay or acknowledge_receipt) is evicted when a new key arrives, typed in Applied::receipts_evicted and Session::receipt_stats() {held, capacity, pending, unacknowledged, evicted}; a pending receipt and a committed one adopted by reconcile/drain that no result has handed over are NOT evictable, a table full of those answers receipts_full before any work starts; room is checked before the provider runs and the eviction happens when the receipt is stored, so a failing submit evicts nothing; an evicted key replays as stale_revision (the revision moved), never a second application; Session::acknowledge_receipt(key) hands an adopted receipt over (receipt_not_held / outcome_unknown / receipt_mismatch typed otherwise)

R5 diverged commit (82a97b4): a receipt that disagrees (binding / revision / base, type Disagreement) keeps the commit pending, listed by Session::diverged() and ReconcileReport::diverged_keys, and reconcile, drain and retries never resolve it; operator commands Session::discard_diverged(key) (drops the draft, document untouched, possibly behind the authority so the next commit answers stale_revision) and Session::resync_diverged(key, authority_document_bytes) (replaces the document with the authority document at the receipt revision: bytes bounded by the folio input and node budgets, parsed by folio, must be this document at the receipt revision with every raster asset present in the source manifest; typed AuthorityFault TooLarge / Invalid / ReadOnly / WrongDocument / WrongRevision / MissingAsset; property revision vector restarts at 0); both re-look the authority up first and answer not_diverged / receipt_not_held / outcome_unknown / grant_revoked / canceled without changing anything; one Observe frame each; DivergenceReport {resolution Discarded|Resynced, revision_before/after, draft_revision, authority receipt, disagreement}

R5 V4 on the crate (82a97b4): crate-level deny(clippy::arithmetic_side_effects) with all 16 flagged sites made checked/saturating (V4-01); set_previews total uses checked_add against the running aggregate before keeping an image, resync_diverged bounds bytes before parsing (V4-02); seed_revisions and mask_property are exhaustive over chronicle Property x folio NodeKind with no wildcard (a new variant fails to compile) and chronicle_property_table_matches_the_session_seed compares the seed with what chronicle itself accepts for every node/property pair including a page spread and an unsupported layer; DESCRIPTOR v4 qualifies the streaming-save memory claim to RAW assets (codec assets are read and encoded whole by the package writer: stream.rs read_blob + encode_blob) and cites a test for each strong claim (V4-07)

R5 negative paths (82a97b4): receipts_full (RefuseWhenFull and all-unacknowledged), receipt_mismatch + diverged, proposal_inconsistent (foreign document id, forged property revision), drain(0) abandoned-not-dropped, not_diverged, receipt_not_held, authority_document_* refusals

decisions: Lazy open is built from package's public API only (PackageReader + EntryMeta data offsets + a second cursor over one shared stream); package has no lazy into_opened, so the document/opaque/unlisted classification and tile-digest-vs-manifest check mirror package's into_opened strictness in src/source.rs
Previews are written only when they describe the revision being written; host-supplied previews are accepted only for the current revision
Grant action for set_previews is Action::Save (a new Action variant would break exhaustive matches in kernel-bindings)
No new SessionError variants: stale previews reuse StaleRevision, invalid previews reuse Package(PreviewMismatch)/TooManyEntries/TotalTooLarge

R3: supersedes 'No new SessionError variants' - a distinct code (proposal_not_derived) for a successor that is not the live document plus the declared writes, so callers can tell it from proposal_inconsistent (wrong document or revision)

R3: lineage is checked in the session (not delegated to the provider): both documents are compared with the declared revision-update properties neutralised; chronicle's property table is mirrored locally (mask_property) because chronicle keeps value/set private

Streaming save keeps the post-save destination reopen: it is how the written file becomes the new lazy source; the package already re-verified the temp, so the manifest document_id/revision check there is a cheap second guard

R5: 'unacknowledged' is the only coherent meaning of the review's 'never silent loss of an unacknowledged receipt': a pending receipt, or a committed one the caller was never handed (adopted by reconcile/drain). Everything handed back through a submit result, replay or acknowledge_receipt is acknowledged and evictable, oldest first

R5: evicting a committed receipt cannot cause a second application: a changed commit advances the revision so a late retry fails the expected-revision check (stale_revision) before the authority is asked, and a no-change key re-evaluates to no-change

R5: 'resolve' for a diverged commit is resync to the authority document (host supplies the bytes, session validates), not 'adopt the draft': CommitReceipt carries no document digest, so adopting a draft against a receipt whose binding or revision disagrees could silently fork content from the authority; discard is the other explicit path. The CommitPort trait was not extended (would break kernel-bindings' port implementation)

R5: chronicle-exported revision seeding: the session brief does not specify it and chronicle (not editable by this lane) exports no property table. Mitigation inside the crate: exhaustive matches plus a cross-check test against chronicle's own acceptance. Request to the chronicle owner: export the addressable (NodeKind, Property) table or a seed/mask helper so the session mirror can be deleted (CX-CAP-001)

CX-CAP-001 resolved (supersedes the R3 'mirrored locally' and R5 'chronicle-exported revision seeding' decisions): chronicle owns the addressability table (PROPERTIES, addressable, seed_revisions, mask_property); the session keeps no copy. The session -> chronicle edge was already allowed (root Cargo.toml metadata) and already a dependency, so no Operator edge decision was needed
known_gaps: open is O(file) in I/O: PackageReader::open CRC-verifies every entry (bounded memory); no way to skip it with the current package API
post-save verification (VerifyMismatch) leaves the newly written file in place and does not advance saved_revision

idempotency table is in memory only; the authority's receipt store is the durable one; an evicted receipt is gone from the session (the authority's store still holds it) and its key answers stale_revision, not a replay
cancel-acknowledgement bound is not separately timed (operations are synchronous, cancel is polled at entry, in provider/read loops and before commit)
resolver in session-consumer grants everything: example stand-in only

export_checkpoint buffers the whole package (in-memory Checkpoint by contract); a zstd or shuffle_zstd source asset is read and encoded whole by the package writer in both passes, so save peak grows with the largest codec blob (claim qualified in DESCRIPTOR v4; no memory bound tested for codec assets)

resync_diverged trusts the host to pass the authority's real document bytes: it checks document id, receipt revision, folio validity, budgets and asset presence, but a receipt carries no document digest to compare content
session-consumer example does not exercise acknowledge_receipt / discard_diverged / resync_diverged (library tests do)
